To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a technique to quantify variance in the reliability estimates obtained from existing architecture-based reliability analysis techniques, which could be used to assess the risk associated with these reliability estimates, and to identify appropriate variance reduction strategies.

we have proposed an approach to quantify the variance associated with the reliability estimate of a software application, and have illustrated how the approach can be used to identify the components that contribute the most to the risk of the application.

(a) our technique generates analytical functions that express the mean and the standard deviation of application reliability as functions of the means and standard deviations of the component reliabiities and the architecture of the application, and that (b) these functions are useful in evaluating the impact of individual component reliabilities on the mean and variance in application reliability, which in turn helps in identifying the components that contribute most to the variance in application reliabilty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
quantifying the risk associated with an application reliability estimate, and our technique is the first of its kind.

the variance in the mean of an application reliability estimate depends on the variance in the reliabilities of its components as well as the architecture of the application.

we present a technique to quantitatively evaluate the reliability of an application based upon its architecture.
we present a novel approach to quantify the variance of application reliability based on the application architecture.
the proposed architecture-based reliability assessment technique can be used to obtain the mean and the standard deviation of the reliability of an application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variance in the mean reliability estimate of an embedded system application can be significantly reduced by identifying the components with large variances and reducing their variances.

the variance of the reliability estimate of the application is not only a function of the variances of the individual components, but also a function of the architectural characteristics of an application.
the variance in the mean application reliability is not always proportional to the variance in the component reliabilities.
